title: Dumas inquest ordered
article: The province's chief medical examiner has called an inquest into the shooting death of a young man in the North End in 2005.
Matthew Adam Joseph Dumas, 18, was shot by police the afternoon of Jan. 31, 2005, on Dufferin Avenue.
Earlier this month, an Ontario Crown attorney ruled the officer who shot Dumas was acting in self-defence and should not face criminal charges.
Manitoba Justice officials had said an inquest could not be called until a decision had been made regarding criminal charges.
Cops had been trying to track down suspects in an earlier break-in in East Kildonan when they approached a group of young people on Dufferin the day of the shooting.
Police say Dumas fled on foot when they tried to question him and allegedly lunged at a cop with a screwdriver after being ordered to drop it.
The young man's family denies the claims, saying Dumas was simply wiping pepper-spray from his eyes.
He was shot twice and died of a gunshot wound to the abdomen after undergoing emergency surgery at Health Sciences Centre.

The inquest is mandatory under the provincial Fatalities Inquiries Act because Dumas was killed by police. It will seek to determine the circumstances of his death and whether anything can be done to prevent similar deaths.
The date and location of the inquest were not released.
